layers.h21: The wallpaper has to slot in between the desktop picture and the desktop icons.
layers.p1: macOS has no “set a live wallpaper” API. What actually works is pinning a borderless window to CGWindowLevelForKey(.desktopIconWindow) − 1 — right above the desktop picture and right below the icons — then making it follow every Space and ignore mouse events.
layers.div8: The “cover icons” switch uses +2, not +1. One level above the icons lives a WindowServer window that occupies the top ~122px of the screen. Ordering within a level isn’t ours to decide, and in practice it sits in front of us — which pressed a white strip across the top of the wallpaper. Found by running it on real hardware; you cannot see this by reading code.
renderers.div2: // The entire format definition for a layered wallpaper { "layers": [ { "image": "sky.png", "depth": 0.0 }, // farthest, barely moves { "image": "hills.png", "depth": 0.45 }, { "image": "tree.png", "depth": 1.0 } // nearest, moves most ] }
power.h21: When nobody can see it, it doesn’t draw a single frame.
power.p1:
This is where a weekend wallpaper hack and a finished product actually differ. Every pause and throttle
        decision lives in one governor; the renderers decide nothing on their own — so “why did my wallpaper stop?”
        always has exactly one answer, and it’s in the log.
power.div3: Screen fully covered by a windowThe biggest win of the lot. Front-to-back window order tells us whether we are really hidden. On by default.
power.div4: Lock screen / display sleep / system sleepOptional low-latency prewarm keeps only the media pipeline ready while the picture stays paused; system sleep always stops everything.
power.div5: Low Power ModeFollows the system switch — someone who turns on Low Power Mode wants the background to go quiet.
power.div6: Running on batteryPause, or drop to a lower frame rate and keep playing. Your choice.
power.div7: Frame cap for web wallpapersWe take over requestAnimationFrame directly — the page cannot route around it, and we are not relying on it to behave.
audio.p1: Hann window, real FFT, logarithmic banding, peak-decay smoothing — packed into the 128 values a wallpaper page expects. You can pick the input device in Settings, with a live spectrum bar right next to it so you can tell at a glance whether any signal is arriving. Off by default, so nothing asks for microphone access unless you turn it on.
audio.div2: Being honest: the wallpaper spectrum cannot hear what your system is playing. It samples an input device — without a loopback driver like BlackHole you get room noise from the microphone, not the song. That's the precondition for this path, and it's on you to meet it. The pet's “dance to music” takes a different route: a Core Audio process tap (macOS 14.2+) that captures only music, video and browser processes, with no virtual audio device required. The two are independent; both analyse locally in real time and never record, save or upload anything.
import.h21: Bring your Wallpaper Engine collection to the Mac.
import.p1:
The command-line converter only reads Wallpaper Engine files already on your machine — no network,
        no Steam, nothing downloaded. Tested against 8 real items totalling 713 MB: 8 of 8 converted.
import.td2: webm / VP9 transcoded to H.264 automatically<small>AVFoundation cannot decode either codec, so transcoding is required</small>
import.td4: The JS interface those pages expect is filled in by a compatibility shim<small>Property listeners, random file requests and audio callbacks are all there</small>
import.td6: Ones with embedded video are extracted automatically<small>Pure scenes have to be pre-rendered to video on the Windows side — supporting them as-is would mean rewriting somebody else’s entire renderer</small>
import.td8: Windows executables<small>Nothing to be done here</small>
import.div2: # Install the dependency and build the converter brew install ffmpeg cd Tools/swaylume-import && swift build -c release # Point it at your local content folder; it writes .swaylume packages .build/release/swaylume-import <your path> -o ~/Desktop/out # Drag the .swaylume files from out/ into Swaylume
import.div3: Converted results are for your own use. Copyright in the original wallpapers stays with their authors — the tool only changes the container format, and that changes nothing about ownership.
paths.h21: Wherever you’re coming from, that’s where Swaylume starts.
paths.p1:
Setting your first live wallpaper, bringing a Windows collection across, or publishing your own work are
        not the same task. So the three routes are separate here, instead of everyone being dropped into one README.
paths.h31: Pick a live wallpaper, put it on your desktop.
paths.p2: Download a `.swaylume` from the catalogue and drag it into the app. Video, images, web and layered wallpapers each get their own native renderer.
paths.h32: Bring your collection; don’t start over.
paths.p3: The converter only reads Wallpaper Engine projects already on your computer — no Steam login, no downloads. Video and web types are supported first, and Scene has a documented pre-render route.
paths.h33: Make one, and put it on other people’s desktops.
paths.p4: Start with the zero-cost catalogue: a clear format, checksums, version history and a visible review trail. Until uploads open properly, the risk doesn’t get pushed onto creators.
wallpapers.h21: Swaylume doesn’t bundle a content library. You choose the material.
wallpapers.p1: Any mp4, image or HTML file can be dragged straight in. Below are a few places people go — we don’t host, resell or vet anything on these sites, we’re only pointing at the road.
wallpapers.p2: Terms checked line by line: free for commercial use, no attribution required, modification allowed. The in-app source list only carries this tier.
wallpapers.div2: Pixabay video ↗ Filter by resolution for 4K; searching for “live wallpaper” or “loop” turns up plenty of ready-made loops. Pixabay Content License: free for commercial use, no attribution required, modification allowed; redistributing or selling content on a standalone basis is not.
wallpapers.div3: Pexels video ↗ Generally high quality, filterable by orientation and resolution. Pexels License: free to use, no attribution required, modification allowed; redistributing on other stock or wallpaper platforms is not, nor is selling unaltered copies.
wallpapers.p3: Most anime- and game-styled live wallpapers live on sites like these. They do not label licensing item by item, so check before you use anything.
wallpapers.div4: These links are not an endorsement. Swaylume has no connection to these sites, takes no part in running them, and cannot vouch for the licensing, quality or safety of what they host. Confirm the licence before you download — copyright in derivative work (anime and game characters and so on) belongs to the original creators, and using something on your own machine is not the same as redistributing it. If something is wrong with one of these sites, open an issue and we’ll drop it.
wallpapers.div5: Free to download for yourself ≠ free to submit. Plenty of free stock sites allow you to download and use their material but forbid redistribution — Pexels explicitly forbids redistributing “on other stock photo or wallpaper platforms”, and a wallpaper catalogue is exactly that. Changing the container format does not count as “applying creative effort”, so please don’t submit this material to the catalogue.
trust.h21: Your desktop shouldn’t become somebody’s cloud asset library.
trust.p1:
A live wallpaper can reach a lot of local files, so Swaylume’s default posture is: ask for fewer permissions,
        keep less data, promise less. What can be done is done properly; what can’t is stated plainly.
trust.p2: Wallpapers, bookmarks, import history and diagnostics all stay on your Mac. Nothing is uploaded automatically, and there are no ad-tracking scripts.
trust.p3: Desktop window levels, multi-Space behaviour, the power strategy and file access all use documented macOS capabilities, keeping the App Store route open.
trust.strong3: Diagnostics you can take with you.
trust.p4: Hit a black screen or a compatibility problem and you can export a redacted local report. It contains state and errors, not your wallpaper files.
trust.p5: Windows application-type wallpapers and native Scene rendering are not promised. Scene has a legitimate video pre-render path instead.
trust.contact: Contact: for questions, to report workshop content, or for copyright and takedown matters, email futureback399@gmail.com. Workshop content is hosted by its submitters — we only maintain the index, but we act on reports.
trust.analytics: About this site: this web page uses Cloudflare Web Analytics to count visits. It sets no cookies, does no cross-site tracking, and builds no profile of individual visitors — we only want to know how many people came and where from. The points above describe the app; this one describes the website.
x.p1:
Swaylume is not affiliated with, authorised by, or endorsed by Wallpaper Engine, its developers, or any
      third-party wallpaper platform. Product names are mentioned only to describe compatibility; trademarks
      belong to their respective owners.
      The converter processes files you already have, on your own computer.

js.gov2.m: occlusion: screen fully covered by an opaque window

faq.h2: The things you probably want settled before you download.
faq.q2: Can I use my own videos or images?
faq.q1: Is it going to drain my battery?
faq.a1: By default it doesn’t draw a single frame when nobody can see it. A fully covered screen, lock screen, display sleep, system sleep and Low Power Mode each have their own pause reason, with automatic resume on wake; on battery you can pause or lower the frame rate. The optional “Zero-latency unlock (Prewarm)” mode still pauses animation and media, keeping only the video pipeline and web process ready for a faster unlock at the cost of a little extra memory. It never prewarms during system sleep, and the app explains the trade-off before enabling it. Every decision lives in one governor, so “why did my wallpaper stop?” always has exactly one answer — and it’s in the log.
faq.a2: Yes — just drag them into the window. Video: mp4 / mov / m4v (H.264 or HEVC). Images: the usual formats plus GIF. Web wallpapers: HTML / WebGL. webm / VP9 will not play directly and must be transcoded first — AVFoundation cannot decode either codec, which is a platform limitation.
faq.q3: How does it compare to Wallpaper Engine?
faq.a3: Honestly, each has its strengths. It has what we don’t: millions of Workshop items, native Scene rendering, a mature editor. We have what it doesn’t: a different wallpaper per Space (not possible on Windows), automatic switching at sunrise and sunset, and a noticeably more serious power strategy. It also has no macOS version — and the collection you already have can come across with the converter.
faq.q4: macOS blocked the first launch. Is the app broken?
faq.a4: No. This build isn’t notarised by Apple yet — notarisation needs a paid developer account. macOS says it “cannot verify the developer”; open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Security and click “Open Anyway” once. All clicks, no Terminal, and only the first time. Full steps are in the download section.
faq.q5: Does it upload any of my data?
faq.a5: No. Wallpapers, bookmarks, import history and diagnostics all stay on your Mac. Nothing is uploaded automatically and there are no ad-tracking scripts. The only network activity is fetching the wallpaper catalogue index when you refresh it yourself; don’t refresh and it never goes online. Diagnostic reports are exported only when you ask, and contain state and errors, not your wallpaper files.
faq.a6: macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon and Intel alike (universal binary). Multiple displays and AirPlay secondary screens have both been tested on real hardware.
faq.feedback: Not answered here? This is a beta, and your question is probably somebody else’s too — open an issue and the answer will end up in this section.
details.title: Technical details and where to find wallpapers — Swaylume
details.description: How audio reactivity works, three ways to get started, where to find live wallpapers and what each site's licence allows, privacy and compatibility limits, and answers to common questions.
ex.h2: Things you can do without opening settings.
ex.p: Four global shortcuts, available while any app is in front. They use the system’s hotkey registration, so they need no Accessibility permission — installing a wallpaper app shouldn’t hand it the ability to read everything you type.
ex.f1d: The settings window can be made semi-transparent so the wallpaper shows through. At zero it is fully opaque, which is the default.
ex.f2d: It fetches one version file and compares. Nothing is sent back. You can turn it off, or skip a particular build.
ex.note: If another app has taken a shortcut, you are told. A failed registration doesn’t fail silently — that row is flagged in settings instead of leaving you pressing keys wondering what broke.
fmt.title: Make a Swaylume wallpaper — the .swaylume package format
fmt.description: Build a live wallpaper that runs in Swaylume: folder layout, every manifest.json field, how adjustable parameters are encoded, the depth model for layered wallpapers, and what to check before submitting.
fmt.h2: Making one is simpler than you think.
fmt.p: A .swaylume is just a folder — macOS registers it as a bundle, so Finder shows it as a single file. Inside: one manifest saying what this is, and a content/ folder with the material. That’s it. No build step, no SDK, no account to register.
fmt.s1p: preview.jpg is optional — leave it out and Swaylume picks a cover frame from the material itself (for video it skips black frames and takes the one with the most going on). What goes in content/ depends on type.
fmt.s2p: Four required fields, everything else optional. The reader ignores fields it doesn’t recognise, so extras are never an error.
fmt.table: FieldRequiredNotesformatVersionRequiredAlways 1 for now. The app refuses packages newer than it supportstitleRequiredDisplay nametypeRequiredvideo / web / image / layeredentryRequiredEntry file, relative to content/authorCreditShown in the library and the inspectorpreviewPreview image, relative to the package rootfillModefill / fit / stretch / centerDefaults to fillmutedDefaults to trueOnly meaningful for material with audiopropertiesUser-adjustable parametersOnly used by web wallpapers — see belowsourceNoteProvenance noteDisplay only, no logic depends on it
fmt.s3h: Let people tune your wallpaper from the inspector.
fmt.s3p: Web wallpapers only. Whatever you declare in the manifest is what shows up in Swaylume’s inspector — switches, sliders, colours, file pickers, text fields. Values reach the page the moment the user drags, with no reload.
fmt.ptable: caseType of _0How it appearsboolBoolSwitchnumber{ value, min, max }SlidertextStringText fieldcolorString, "r g b" — three 0…1 floatsColour pickerfile{ fileType }File pickerdirectory{ fileType }Folder picker
fmt.note1: number takes an object for _0, not a bare value. A slider can’t be drawn without knowing its range — Wallpaper Engine sliders show up as 0…1, 0…100, 0…359, 0…1000 in the wild. Without the range the inspector has to guess, and every drag lands in the wrong place.
fmt.note2: For file / directory you only write fileType. Once the user picks something in Swaylume, the app fills in bookmark and displayName — that’s a security-scoped bookmark, it lives only in the local library file, it is not part of the package format, and export strips it (it carries your folder names, which shouldn’t travel).
fmt.note3: Pages written for Wallpaper Engine mostly work unchanged. These values reach the page as { name: { value, type } } through wallpaperPropertyListener.applyUserProperties, matching Wallpaper Engine’s contract. Property listeners, random file picking and audio callbacks are filled in by the compatibility layer.
fmt.s4h: 2.5D parallax: a few images, each with a depth.
fmt.s4p: Set type to layered and put a layers.json plus your cut-out images in content/. depth runs 0…1: 0 is farthest and barely moves, 1 is nearest and tracks the pointer most. The relative motion between layers is where the depth comes from — no video decoding, almost no power draw.
fmt.s5h: How this format is allowed to change.
fmt.s5p: Only a breaking change touches formatVersion. Put differently: a package you build today won’t stop working because we added a field tomorrow.
fmt.rules:
New fields are always optional.The reader must ignore fields it doesn’t recognise rather than fail. That’s a hard rule, not advice.
formatVersion only rises on a breaking change.Adding a field isn’t breaking. If it ever does rise, old packages still load — they just miss the new capability.
The old extension still works.Packages exported as .livewall before the rename hold the same v1 format inside; Finder association and import both still work. Only new exports use .swaylume.
Writer and reader are one contract.The converter and the app’s import path change together. Letting one side move first means exporting packages you can’t read back.
fmt.foot: Run it locally before you submit. Drag the .swaylume straight into Swaylume: it should play, and every parameter in the inspector should do what you meant. The catalog repo’s CI re-checks structure and checksums, but it cannot check whether the thing looks right — only you can.

h.hero.title: Your desktop, alive.
h.hero.sub: Video, WebGL and 2.5D wallpapers that live right beneath your desktop icons. Built for the Mac from the ground up.
foot.apple: Mac and macOS are trademarks of Apple Inc. Swaylume is an independently developed app and is not affiliated with Apple.
h.statement: Not a recorded video. Not a web gimmick. Your desktop, breathing.
h.gallery.title: Pick one. Your desktop does the rest.
h.gallery.sub: What’s playing on that display is a wallpaper that ships with the app, not a promo animation. Pick one and watch it change.
h.gallery.caption: 26 built-in wallpapers out of the box, plus your own videos, images and web pages.
h.under.title: Beneath your icons. Behind your windows.
h.under.sub: Your wallpaper lives in the layer between the desktop picture and the desktop icons. Windows work as usual, icons stay clickable, and nothing has to make room.
h.under.step1: Wallpaper slides in under the icons
h.kinds.title: Three kinds of wallpaper. Each on its own path.
h.kinds.sub: Video goes to the hardware decoder, web pages to WebKit, layered images to Core Animation. Nobody makes do with somebody else’s engine.
h.kinds.web.title: WebGL, tuned by hand.
h.kinds.web.text: The sliders a wallpaper declares show up in the inspector. Drag one — it changes the wallpaper above, through the same interface the app uses.
h.kinds.video.title: Video, looped seamlessly.
h.kinds.video.text: No black frame and no stutter at the seam. 4K60 goes to the GPU, so the CPU barely notices.
h.kinds.layer.title: 2.5D, almost no power.
h.kinds.layer.text: A few images, each with its own depth, shift with your pointer. Move it over the picture to see.
h.pet.title: From a photo to a desktop pet.
h.pet.sub: Give it a few photos of your cat. Swaylume measures the coat, the build and the tail, and grows a pixel cat that matches. It lives on your desktop and never steals focus.
h.pet.hint: Move your pointer in, then click it
h.pet.p1.d: Coat colors, head-to-body ratio and leg length are all measured from the photos, not picked from a template.
h.pet.p2.d: It wanders, grooms and naps on its own — and walks over to your pointer when it gets curious.
h.pet.p3.d: Pat its head and it squints and purrs; click it and it meows. ⌥⌘C calls it over to your pointer.
h.multi.title: Every display, its own.
h.multi.sub: Give each display its own wallpaper, use the same one everywhere, or stretch a single picture across all of them. Every Space can be different too.
h.multi.label: Multi-display mode
h.multi.caption: Video and images can span right away; a web wallpaper has to declare span support, otherwise each display draws its own copy.
h.power.title: When no one’s looking, not a single frame.
h.power.s0.d: It follows your display’s refresh rate, or the cap you set.
h.power.s1.t: Covered by a window, paused at once
h.power.s1.d: The biggest power saver of all, on by default.
h.power.s2.d: Follows the system switch; on battery you can choose to pause instead.
h.power.s3.d: When the Mac sleeps, nothing is left running in the background.
h.keys.title: No need to open Settings.
h.keys.sub: Four global shortcuts that work whichever app is in front. Try holding ⌥ and ⌘ on this page.
h.keys.note: They use the system’s shortcut registration, so no Accessibility permission is needed — a wallpaper app shouldn’t be able to read everything you type.
h.we.title: Coming from Wallpaper Engine?
h.we.sub: A command-line tool converts the video and web wallpapers already on your machine into packages Swaylume can use. No network, no Steam.
h.get.title: Bring your desktop to life.
h.get.sub: Free. No bundled extras, no promotional add-ons.
h.get.meta: macOS 14 or later · Apple silicon and Intel · dmg
h.get.blocked: Blocked by macOS the first time? That’s expected
h.get.b1: Double-click Swaylume and let it be refused once. Don’t skip this — macOS has to record the block before the button below appears.
h.get.b3: Scroll down to Security and find the line saying Swaylume was blocked.
h.get.b4: Click Open Anyway next to it, then confirm.
h.get.after: After that it opens with a normal double-click and won’t ask again. Swaylume isn’t notarized by Apple yet (that requires a paid developer account) — it doesn’t mean anything is wrong with the app.
